name: Chemical EOR (polymer and surfactant flooding)
applications: extra oil from mature waterflooded fields
principle: Chemicals are added to injection water to recover oil that waterflooding leaves behind. Polymers such as hydrolyzed polyacrylamide (HPAM) raise the viscosity of the injected water so it sweeps the reservoir more evenly and water breaks through later. Surfactants lower the interfacial tension between oil and water so trapped oil droplets can move. Alkali-surfactant-polymer (ASP) combines both. Polymer and surfactant performance depends on salinity, temperature, adsorption on the rock and injectivity, so candidates are screened in the laboratory and by core flooding before a field pilot.

performance.metric: incremental recovery after 0.35 PV HPAM polymer slug following waterflood, light-oil coreflood
performance.basis: HPAM 500-1,500 ppm (1,000 ppm recommended) in brine of roughly 2,800 ppm salinity at 70 C; waterflood alone 38.7% OOIP; about 22% of residual oil in place; 500 ppm avoided plugging (FR 1.1, RRF near 1); laboratory coreflood only

performance.metric: oil recovery factor after 3-year waterflood plus 17-year polymer flood, Air Benakat formation model, South Sumatra (simulation)
performance.basis: CMG-STARS, 1,500 ppm polymer after 3 years of waterflooding; 59.86% homogeneous model, 45.83/69.27/80.46% for Lorenz coefficient 0.2/0.4/0.6; simulation only

source.note: Ramadhan et al., Heterogeneity Effect on Polymer Injection: a Study of Sumatra Light Oil, SCOG 46(1): 45-58, 2023 (LEMIGAS SCOG, CC BY-SA 4.0), Effect on Oil Recovery Factor

performance.metric: incremental recovery from microemulsion ASP plus polymer drive after waterflood, Bentheimer coreflood
performance.basis: 2% surfactant A + 0.85% Na2CO3 (ASP) with 2,200 ppm polymer; 0.15 PV ASP slug then 1.5 PV polymer drive at 85 C; waterflood alone 38.21% Soi, total 95.93% Soi, i.e. 93.41% of remaining oil; salinity conditioned by synthetic softened brine preflush; laboratory only

reference_plants.name: PETRONAS Carigali and Shell Malaysia EOR program, Baram Delta (Sarawak) and North Sabah PSCs, offshore Malaysia
reference_plants.capacity: HOA aims to lift production by 90,000-100,000 boe/d across the Baram Delta and North Sabah fields, raising average recovery factor from 36% to 50% and extending field life beyond 2040; technology deployed at North Sabah flagged as possibly the world's first field-scale offshore chemical EOR process

source.note: Offshore magazine, PETRONAS, Shell consider first-ever field-scale chemical EOR offshore Malaysia, 11 November 2011 (status as of that source; read 28 October 2026)

advantages: Polymer flooding is an established way to improve a waterflood
Palm-oil MES is a locally sourced, biodegradable surfactant option in Southeast Asia
Laboratory screening is cheap relative to field trials
limitations: Polymer viscosity falls with salinity, temperature and shear
Adsorption and injectivity losses can cut recovery below bulk-viscosity predictions
Surfactant results shown here are laboratory core floods, not field results
